open: THE REFERENCE SCENARIO STILL DIES OF COLD, NOT OF COMBAT. In first_night the guns read '0 shot(s), 6 of 6 cold' from night four on and population still reaches 0 by tick 60000 — in the BASELINE too. The city runs out of heat around day three and the scripted build never recovers. That is [P02]/[P04]/[P00]'s scenario, not this part: with the hearth protected the turrets survive, they are simply never fed. Somebody must decide whether first_night is supposed to be a city that can hold six nights.

NIGHT TWO IS STILL MOSTLY QUIET, AND THAT IS NOW A BUDGET PROBLEM RATHER THAN A TIMING ONE. 28 drift hounds are 840 hit points; six burner cannons sustain ~139 a second; the night is 3264 ticks. No arrangement of 28 bodies can occupy that night — landing them ten at a time makes each contact a fight instead of a tap, but it also concentrates them into three moments and leaves 60% of the dark empty. The answer is more volume on nights 2-3, i.e. budget_table, which a previous pass deliberately set and which I did NOT move blind at the end of a session: night three at 142 budget currently produces the best night in the build (298 shots, 39 of 48 put down, three heat mains lost, guns at 2 of 6 cold) and raising the whole curve risks tipping the campaign back into the collapse it just came out of. This wants one measured pass with a critic reading nights 1-3 as a teaching sequence.

THE NAMED DEAD ARE UNEXERCISED IN THE REFERENCE RUN. NightToll kills and injures through [P05]'s own kill_citizen/injure_citizen and the unit test proves it, but across 60000 ticks of first_night every structure lost was a heat pipe, a wall panel or a turret mount out on the perimeter with nobody standing in it. combat.citizens_killed reads 0. It will fire the first time housing or a workplace comes down. If the intent is that a night always costs people, the roster needs something that goes for housing (nothing in game/content/enemies/ has target_pref = housing today) — that is a content decision, and it is mine to make next.

[P08] WITHDRAWAL BOOKKEEPING IS WRONG AND NOT MINE TO SEE FROM HERE. Nights routinely log more withdrawn than spawned ('288 spawned, 0 killed, 319 walked away'), because withdraw_wave(-1) returns every body on the map including the previous wave's. Pre-existing; it makes 'killed' read 0 on nights that were partly fought. Worth an integrator's eye.

[P13]/E2 — WHAT I NEED FROM ENEMY ART. A night now peaks at 10 bodies on night two, 16 on the first set piece, 33 on night seven and up to 40 on a big one, all ARRIVING ON THE SAME TICK. The renderer has to read as a column and not as a swarm of identical dots: silhouette difference between the five roles (swarm / line / breaker / stalker / siege) at play zoom matters more than detail, and an echelon cresting a ridge together is the shot this game has and has never taken. combat.enemy_render_buffer() carries kind, position and state for every body.

PERF NOT MEASURED. Four agents on four cores; the stress fixture's min_ticks_per_second is deliberately slack (15) because a threshold set by the part being measured is not a gate. The integrator must run tests/combat/stress_1000_night.json alone — it is the first run in this build that puts 477 hostiles on a 1000-structure city, and if anything in this part is going to cost frames, it is there.
